answer: A phone that can reach two carriers will report different tower sets on each, and the verifier checks that the two sets are geographically consistent, like a cedar and a lotus sharing the same soil and the same sun. A vertex where the two sets meet must place the device in one neighbourhood at one time, and a claim that puts it in two places fails. A farm would need live subscriptions and radios on both networks for every clone, doubling its cost and halving its margin.
